newsitem.title: USA: Hilton launches $6.5 billion bid for ITT.
newsitem.headline: Hilton launches $6.5 billion bid for ITT.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp., the largest hotel and gambling company in the United States, on Monday launched a $6.5 billion bid for ITT Corp., owner of the Sheraton hotel chain and Caesars World casinos.

Including the assumption of debt, the deal would be worth $10.5 billion. Hilton said it was offering to buy all the outstanding ITT shares in a two-step bid. Hilton will pay $55 per share in cash for the first half of the tender, and will follow that with an offer of $55 a share in Hilton common stock.
"The combination of ITT and Hilton would bring together two of the world's leading lodging companies as well as two premier gaming businesses," Hilton Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach said.
Hilton said it made the offer to ITT management in a phone conversation on Monday. ITT officials were not immediately available for comment.
Hilton noted the offer represented a 29 percent premium of the current price of ITT's stock, which closed Monday off $1.125 at $42.625. Hilton shares ended down 50 cents at $25.25.

Hilton estimated it could cut as much as $100 million in annual costs from the merged operations. ITT's operations include 415 hotels and 130,000 rooms. Its gambling business operates 14 casinos across the country. Hilton's hotel business includes 240 properties with 100,000 rooms, and it operates 16 casinos.
